newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar signs a $500 mln petrochemical venture.
newsitem.headline: Qatar signs a $500 mln petrochemical venture.

text.p: Qatar on Wednesday signed a $500 million joint venture deal with Norwegian and French companies to set up a petrochemical project, a cabinet minister said.

Minister of Energy and Industry Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah said Qatar Vinyl Company (QVC) would produce 338,000 tonnes of ethylene dichloride (EDC), 200,000 tonnes of vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) and 260,000 tonnes of caustic soda (NaOH) a year.
It might be expanded within a few years to produce polyvinyl chloride (PVC), he added.

State-run Qatar General Petroleum Corporation will own 25.5 percent, Qatar Petrochemicals Company, a subsidiary of QGPC, will have 31.9 percent of stakes while Norway's Norsk Hydro SDB and France's Elf Atochem SA will hold 29.7 percent and 12.9 percent of shares respectively.
Attiyah, who signed the deal with representatives of the Norwegian and French companies, told reporters the project would go on stream in the first half of 2000.
The new company will utilise ethylene produced by Qatar Petrochemicals Company as feedstock and will be located next to it in the area of Messaieed, 48 km (30 miles) south of Doha.
It will be the oil and gas-rich state's fourth petrochemical venture designed to transform its abundant gas reserves - the third largest in the world - into cash.
Qatar Petrochemicals Company (QAPCO), the country's first, has been producing ethylene and low density polyethyelene (LDPE) since 1982.
The two others -- Qatar Fuel Additive Company (Qafac) and a Qatar Clean Energy Company (Qacenco) were set up last year to produce methonol and methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE).
QVC will target Southeast Asian and Far East regions as its main market.
"The Middle East countries presently have no significant room for EDC and other products, but they are developing", said a QGPC official.
Norsk Hydro is also a 25 percent partner in Qatar Fertilisers Company (Qafco), and Elf Atochem holds 10 percent of QAPCO.
